sentences.text: Shri Manish Datt, learned Senior Advocate with Shri Ritwik Parashar counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Bhaskar Pandey, learned P.L. for the respondent/State.
Heard on question of admission.
This revision is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No. 7575/19, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Petitioner has been convicted for an offence under Section 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 and sentenced to undergo RI for 1 years with fine of Rs.
2,000/- also with default stipulation.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 and
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to case, complainant was the Food Inspector.
On 18.08.1994, he was conducted an inspection in Chandrakala Sweets situated at Wright Town Jabalpur.
On inspection, he found that petitioner, who was the owner of the said shop was there and sweets and namkeen were being made under his instruction.
Complainant-Food Inspector had inspected the same.
Thereafter, he had also inspected oil which was used for making the same, for which he had purchased 375 gm sunflower oil, after getting its receipt from the shop owner.

Thereafter, sample was sent to the lab for examination, in which it is found that the said sample was below standard, therefore, he has filed a complaint under Section 20(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954, after getting sanction from the concerned department.
The learned trial Court has framed the charges for the aforesaid offences and petitioner-accused abjured his guilt.
The learned trial Court has also recoded the statement of petitioner under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
In trial, 2 CRR-2080-2019 after considering the material, available on recorded the learned trial Court found petitioner guilty for the aforesaid offence and sentenced him as aforesaid.

Being aggrieved, an appeal has also been preferred by the petitioner before 18th ASJ, Jabalpur,
which has also been dismissed by the Appellant Judge.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the conviction imposed by the learned trial Court as well as Appellate Court is bad in law as there is no evidence available against the petitioner.
The petitioner had not manufactured the aforesaid oil, in fact he had purchased the same.

There is no Kamal Kumar Goklani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199795357/
1 evidence on record to indicate that the petitioner was involved in the said offence.

sentences.text: The evidence which has been given by the prosecution is very week and on the basis of the same petitioner can not be convicted.
The learned trial court as well as Appellate Court has over looked the provision of Section 9-B and also the petitioner was deprived from his rights provided under Section 13(2) of the Act 1954.

The petitioner also took the defence of Section 468 and 470 of Cr.P.C. as the complaint filed by the complainant after lapse of prescribed period but the learned Courts below did not consider the same.
Apart from that petitioner is old age person, having more than 59 years of age and he is in jail since 15.04.2019.
He further submits that there are fair chances to succeed in the case.
Final hearing of this revision will take time.
If the petitioner is not released on bail, the purpose of filing this revision will be frustrated.
Therefore, the application filed on behalf of the petitioner may be allowed and the period of his remaining jail sentence may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
On the other hand, the bail application is opposed by counsel for the State.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner.

After hearing rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and from perusal of the record, it appears that the initial case has been filed 3 CRR-2080-2019 against the four accused persons namely Kamal Kumar Goklanei (Petitioner), Chandra Prakash, Yogesh Chandra and Kishan Lal.

During trial, accused Yogesh Chandra and Kishan Lal who were the Chairman and Vice Chairman of the company had discharged from the offences, vide order dated 04.03.2004, passed by this High Court in M.Cr.C. No. 1434/99.

The ground, on the basis the aforesaid accused had been discharged that the Food Inspector had failed to obtain a declaration to the effect that the adulterated substance was purchased and stored in the same condition.
It is also held by the High Court that the aforesaid accused are not responsible for production, quality control and marketing of the company.
So far as other accused namely Chandra Parkash is concerned, he has also been acquitted by the learned Appellate Court by giving the benefit of doubt.
The allegation, which has been made against him that he was the whole seller of the said oil.

The present petitioner has been convicted by the Courts below on the ground that he had failed to prove this fact that he had purchased the adulterated oil from the other accused persons and was using the same in its original condition.
he had also failed to produce any receipt or bill in this regard.
From perusal of statements of complainant, it appears that he has found that the present petitioner had purchased the said oil from the whole seller/accused Chandra Prakash.
It is also reflected from the complaint that during the period of taking sample complainant had opened one pack container of oil.

The learned counsel for the petitioner raised the argument regarding compliance of Section 13(2) of the Act,1954, it appears from the statement of complainant, he has stated in his cross examination that he did not send any notice under Section 13(2) to the accused persons and the same is send by the Local Health Authority, Jabalpur, but from perusal of record there is no documents is found in this regard.
It is also reflected from his statements that he had admitted this fact there is a limited life of such type of food product and he is unable to explain the same.
He is also admitted that 4 CRR-2080-2019 in the report of public analysis it was mentioned by him that "sample is not clear in appearance".

From perusal of judgment passed by trial Court it Kamal Kumar Goklani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199795357/
2 also appears that petitioner had also taken the ground of Sections 468 and 470 of Cr.P.C.
From the above said discussion, prima facie it seems

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that the present petitioner is not the manufacturer of the said adulterated oil
and looking to the statement of complainant/Food Inspector regarding compliance of provision of Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954, this revision is seeking reconsideration.

Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered opinion that it would be appropriate to suspend the custodial sentence awarded to the applicants and grant bail to him.
Consequently, I.A. No. 7575/19 is allowed subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited.
The custodial sentence awarded to the petitioner shall remain suspended during the pendency of this revision.

Petitioner- Kamal Kumar Goklani be released from custody subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
The petitioner shall appear and mark his presence before trial Court on 27.09.2019 and shall continue to do so on all such future dates as may be given in this behalf, during pendency of the matter.
C.c as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR SRIVASTAVA) JUDGE L.R.
